observations: The site header and section navigation wrap a 720px settings content column. Sections switch to a horizontal tab bar at or below 720px, with inline loading and retry states.
inferences: My weekly report can follow this section layout and use the existing Card, Field, Button and Input patterns.
limitations: The settings layout does not currently establish the proposed subscription flow or its access rules.

observations: The neutral shell, Radix colors, typography, hairline borders, restrained radii and field rows are reflected in apps/dashboard/src/lib/styles/tokens.css, radix.css and the Svelte UI components.
limitations: The standalone HTML uses a token subset and system font fallbacks. It reproduces the relevant patterns without including the application shell runtime.

observations: The viewer role has no existing settings section. SiteHeader.svelte links to the first visible section. The organization editor sees block rules, goals, and sharing.
inferences: A new personal section gives an authorized viewer a Settings tab without granting the viewer access to other sections.
limitations: The prototype runs without a session or network. It illustrates the intended UI access boundary only.

observations: Status is off, pending or active; a pending code lasts 15 minutes and is a 43-character base64url token. One request per account per minute across sites (429). The fifth wrong code clears the pending code. Wrong, expired and cleared codes all return 400 invalid_code. Request returns 503 mail_unavailable without SMTP and 502 mail_failed after storing the new code when SMTP refuses it.

Reports cover the previous complete site-local week and are sent after 09:00 on the site's first weekday. The body carries the site name, ISO from/to dates, time zone, visitors, visits, pageviews and {RIVU_BASE_URL}/s/{site_id}. Subjects are fixed per language.
inferences: The settings page can only show one message for an invalid code and must re-read status to learn that a code was voided.
limitations: The API does not return the stored email language, the next send date or the confirmation time.

observations: Mailer::send builds a single text/plain message. Invitation and password reset emails use the same plain-text style.
inferences: An HTML email needs a multipart/alternative change in Mailer::send.

observations: The primary variant uses --accent-solid with --accent-contrast text.
